title: The Value of Sport
summary: We listened to a radio interview with Anthony, who does triathlons, and Sue, who does weightlifting. We learned multi-word verbs for sport and health, like take up, switch off and burn off. Then we asked each other questions and discussed opinions about sport.

grammar.title: Multi-word verbs for sport and health
grammar.explain: A multi-word verb is a verb plus a small word like up, off, on or down. Together they have a new meaning, so learn them as one unit. Some phrases use an adjective + preposition, like hard on and hooked on.
grammar.explain_ar: الفعل المركّب (multi-word verb) هو فعل مع كلمة صغيرة مثل up أو off أو on أو down، ويصبح لهما معاً معنى جديد، لذلك احفظهما كوحدة واحدة. وبعض العبارات تتكوّن من صفة + حرف جر مثل hard on و hooked on.
form: verb + particle: take up, switch off, burn off, build up, come down
verb + particle + object: take up running / burn off calories / build up muscle
verb + object + particle: keep the weight off
switch off from + noun: switch off from work
be + adjective + on: be hard on the knees / be hooked on a sport

examples.en: Anthony took up triathlons in his mid-50s.
examples.note: take up = start a new sport or hobby

examples.en: Weightlifting helps Sue switch off from the stress of her job.
examples.note: switch off = stop thinking about work and relax

examples.en: After a few weeks Sue was hooked on weightlifting.
examples.note: hooked on = loving something and wanting to do it all the time

examples.en: Running can be hard on the knees and ankles.
examples.note: hard on = bad for a part of the body

examples.en: Weightlifting burns off calories and helps to keep the weight off.
examples.note: burn off = use up; keep the weight off = not get heavier again

examples.en: Anthony's friend suggested he come down to the running club.
examples.note: come down = come to a place

mistakes.wrong: Running is hard for the knees.
mistakes.right: Running is hard on the knees.
mistakes.why: The phrase is hard on + part of the body.

mistakes.wrong: I took on tennis last year.
mistakes.right: I took up tennis last year.
mistakes.why: Take up = start a hobby. Take on = accept a job or responsibility.

mistakes.wrong: Swimming helps me switch off of work.
mistakes.right: Swimming helps me switch off from work.

mistakes.wrong: It make you feel happy and you switch off stress.
mistakes.right: It makes you feel happy and helps you switch off.
mistakes.why: He/she/it needs -s in the present simple.

quiz.q: What was the last new hobby you took ___?
quiz.why: Take up = start a new hobby.

quiz.q: Which activities help you switch ___ from work?
quiz.why: Switch off = stop thinking about work and relax.

quiz.q: A one-hour swim can burn ___ 500 calories.
quiz.why: Burn off = use up energy or calories.

quiz.q: What makes people get hooked ___ sports?

quiz.why: Build up = make bigger or stronger little by little.

quiz.q: Should people do sports that are hard ___ the knees?
quiz.why: Hard on + part of the body = bad for it.
